title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's. It is a typed English page, numbered 'H2', headed 'APPENDIX H (Hirsch Method)'. It is evidently from a rational-homotopy preprint by Dennis Sullivan, or a text closely derived from his circle, c. 1973–75, and it sits inside Grothendieck's dossier on half-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures.

The mathematics, in modern language:
(1) Hirsch's lemma. Let G -> E -> M be a principal G-bundle and A a cdga quasi-isomorphic to the forms on M. If H*(G) = Λ(x_1,...,x_n) is exterior on primitive generators, one can form the relative Sullivan algebra (A ⊗ Λ(x_1,...,x_n), D). Here D(1⊗x_i) = c_i⊗1, where c_i is a cocycle representing the characteristic class, i.e. the transgression of x_i (via Chern–Weil or the classifying map). The resulting cdga computes H*(E).
(2) The same construction is applied inductively along a Postnikov tower of principal fibrations K(π, i_n) -> X_{n+1} -> X_n. Each stage is classified by a k-invariant in H^{i_n+1}(X_n; π). The rational de Rham algebra (Sullivan's polynomial forms A_PL) is a strictly commutative cochain model computing rational cohomology. With it, one builds by induction cdgas of 'minimal model type' for every stage. At each step one adjoins a vector space V_n ≅ Hom(π_{i_n} ⊗ Q, Q) of generators in degree i_n. Their differential is a cocycle representing the k-invariant. This yields Sullivan's minimal model of a nilpotent space.

Role in the dossier: Grothendieck's surrounding notes concern Γ^i, Λ^j and divided-power/exterior structures on half-simplicial modules (Dold–Kan, Koszul-type complexes Γ^n -> Γ^{n-1}⊗Φ -> ... -> Λ^n). That is the integral or characteristic-free problem of commutative multiplicative cochain models. Sullivan's rational answer, built from Hirsch extensions, is the natural reference point, and this page was presumably kept as background.
errors: The statement d(1⊗x_i) = c_i⊗1 is a simplification. It holds when the x_i are chosen as transgressive (primitive) generators, e.g. G compact connected over the reals or rationals, and c_i must represent the transgression or characteristic class associated to x_i. In general the differential may need correction terms.
'Same rank and dimension of the homotopy group of K' should be read rationally: one adjoins Hom(π_{i_n}(K) ⊗ Q, Q) in degree i_n. Integral or torsion information is lost.
For i_n = 1, or for non-nilpotent towers, extra hypotheses are needed. Principality of the fibrations, i.e. nilpotence, is what makes the inductive Hirsch extension work.

ideas.what: Hirsch's lemma: the cohomology of a principal bundle is computed by a twisted tensor product A ⊗ Λ(x_i) with d x_i = c_i (transgression).
ideas.modern_name: Hirsch extension / relative Sullivan algebra; Koszul–Cartan–Chevalley theorem for principal bundles
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Hirsch (c. 1953); H. Cartan, Koszul, Chevalley (1950)

ideas.what: Inductive construction of commutative cochain models along a Postnikov tower of principal fibrations, using rational polynomial de Rham forms.
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan minimal model of a nilpotent space; A_PL
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Sullivan (Infinitesimal computations in topology, 1977; preprints c. 1973–75)

missed.claim: Archival/historical point: a typed page of Sullivan's rational-homotopy text (Appendix H on the Hirsch method) is filed within Grothendieck's c. 1975–76 notes on dévissage of half-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures (Γ, Λ). This documents that Grothendieck was reading Sullivan's minimal-model theory while working on commutative or divided-power cochain models. It is not new mathematics.
missed.quote: Using the Hirsch method and the existence of the rational de Rham algebra which is commutative and correctly computes cohomology we can inductively construct differential algebras of the minimal model type
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to the history of Grothendieck's interest in homotopy theory before Pursuing Stacks. It also bears on how his search for integral or characteristic-free commutative models relates to Sullivan's rational theory and to later work on E_∞ and divided-power models (Mandell, Toën, etc.).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard exposition of Hirsch extensions and Sullivan minimal models, apparently from Sullivan's own preprint, not by Grothendieck. Its only interest is archival: it shows that Grothendieck had this text in hand.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed English, not Grothendieck's handwriting; the header 'H2' at top right is a page number of the appendix.
There is a handwritten '2' at bottom left (archive pagination).
The diagram is K -> X_{n+1} with a vertical arrow π_n down to X_n; the transcription's inline arrow is acceptable.
The last line continues on the next page of the original document, not on Grothendieck's next page.
